title: Digital sign-off of flight records
notes: Each saved flight record now has a Sign-off box: the pilot in command enters their name and optional licence number, ticks the acceptance statement and taps Accept and sign. The name, time and a SHA-256 fingerprint of the record are stored with it.

Opening a signed record recomputes the fingerprint and confirms the record is unchanged since sign-off. The sign-off and fingerprint are printed on the PDF, shown on the printout and included in the CSV log.
Signed records are marked in the Flight records list and need the usual two taps to delete.

title: Manifest and flight records
notes: Flight manifest on the W&B page: flight details, crew and passengers with seats and weights, baggage and freight with locations. The manifest fills the station loads automatically (switchable), so the W&B follows the manifest.

Save flight record keeps a dated snapshot of the manifest, the full weight and balance (every weight, arm and moment, the four conditions against their limits and the verdict) and the Perf tab's take-off and landing inputs and results. Records are listed in the W&B side panel.

Each record can be shared as a PDF built on the device (works offline), printed, copied as text or deleted, and carries a pilot-in-command signature line. Export log (CSV) gives one line per flight for a spreadsheet; Export records (JSON) exports everything.
Clear loads also clears the manifest when it is in use.

title: Performance tab: take-off and landing distances
notes: New Perf tab. Enter the aerodrome elevation, QNH, temperature, runway heading and the wind as broadcast on ATIS, AWIS or a METAR, the slope, surface and weight (or take the weight from the W&B tab) and the app reads the POH chart for you: pressure height, head and crosswind components, the take-off safety speed or reference approach speed for that weight, the distance to or from 50 ft and the ground roll, unfactored and with your safety factor, plus a sufficient / insufficient verdict against the runway length you enter.

GA8 charts from GA-FM-04 Section 5: take-off 14° flap, 3° powered-approach landing and power-off landing (with its rate of descent), digitised from the manual's drawing and followed exactly as on paper. The AFM's limits are enforced: no extrapolation above the chart, the lowest scheduled figure below it, 5 kt tailwind to 20 kt headwind, slopes to 2 %, 15 kt demonstrated crosswind warning.

A Load AFM example button fills each chart's worked example so the result can be compared with the manual. The take-off and power-off examples agree within 2 %; the 3° approach chart's printed example is about 10 % shorter than its own guide lines, which the app follows (the conservative reading) – see the note on that page.
Other types show the tab with a note that their charts have not been entered yet. All performance figures are marked unverified until checked against the POH.

title: GA8 weight and balance from the AFM
notes: GA8 W&B template now carries the station arms, fuel arm, cargo-zone limits and CG envelope from the GA8 manual GA-FM-04 (Section 2 limits and Section 6 trim sheets), in kilograms and millimetres from the firewall datum. Seat rows and freighter cargo zones are both listed.

An example GA8 registration, VH-WSM, is seeded once so the tab can be tried straight away. Its empty weight and arm are fictitious (the AFM worked example) and it is marked TEST DATA; delete it from Edit profile when you no longer need it and it stays deleted.
The template figures were transcribed by hand and remain marked unverified: confirm them against the AFM and the aircraft's own weight and balance report.

title: Weight and balance for the C208B and GA8
notes: New W&B tab: set up each registration with its empty weight and arm from the aircraft's weight and balance report, enter loads and fuel, and see zero-fuel, ramp, take-off and landing weights, CG arms, an in-or-out verdict and the envelope plot.
Type templates for the C208B (stations, limits, envelope – unverified, check against the POH) and the GA8 (layout and limits; arms and envelope entered from the AFM).
Registrations and last-used loads are kept on the device and travel with Export / Import.

title: Offline voice recognition (experimental)
notes: Status → Voice → Offline recognition: a one-off 46 MB download lets the app recognise replies, Say procedure and the “hey Aero” wake word on the device with no signal. It only listens for the words the app expects, which also makes it more accurate in engine noise.
The download is kept separately from the app and survives updates; Remove the offline download frees the space.
On Apple devices the microphone is released while the app speaks (switchable) so speech is never muted.
Smoother reading: the speech watchdog no longer restarts an utterance that has already begun, and the pause between challenge and response is a clean sentence break.

Wake-word commands wait for the whole phrase: a phrase the engine cuts short at a pause (“hey Aero, before … start checklist”) is joined with what follows, while an exact checklist name opens at once.
Smoother reading: the audio engine is no longer rebuilt around every line, cue tones release the audio hardware when idle, and the speech engine is only nudged when paused.
Offline engine: the microphone now stays open between lines by default, so replies are heard straight away and the switching click is gone; the accept tone is a soft short tick.
The checklist list no longer hides its last entries behind the voice bar, and it keeps its scroll position when the app refreshes.
Reset returns a checklist to the top; after each tick the checklist scrolls so the next item and those after it stay in view; a newly opened checklist always starts at the top.

title: Editable normal checklists
notes: Every normal checklist can be customised per aircraft: open it and tap Edit to add, change, remove or reorder lines, add notes, or restore the original. Edited checklists show ✎ in the list and “Customised on this device” under the title.
Export / Import on the Status page turns a device's customisations into text an operator can send to pilots, who paste it in.
Abnormal and emergency procedures are not editable.

Charts tab: one-tap links to the Airservices DAP, ERSA and NAIPS pages and to FD Pro, OzRunways or AvPlan if installed, with an aerodrome code for AIP searches. Charts cannot be embedded in the app; use iPad Split View alongside it.
Status → Customised checklists has a switch to use one approach checklist for every favourite (★) aircraft.
User guide brought fully up to date.
Charts tab: DAP and ERSA links now follow Airservices' dated amendment cycle, with the AIP index as a fallback; the Jeppesen button uses the FliteDeck Pro X link name.
Header tabs stay readable in iPad Split View. The Charts tab opens the NAIPS app directly, with the website beside it, and explains where ERSA lives.

title: “Hey Aero” wake word and a custom approach checklist
notes: Wake word (Status → Voice, off by default): with the app on screen, say “hey Aero, landing checklist”, “hey Aero, engine failure in flight”, “hey Aero, status” or “hey Aero, stop”. A red dot by the aircraft name shows it is listening. Uses battery and needs signal on Apple devices.

Custom approach checklist: create or edit your own approach checklist per aircraft from the Status page. It sits under Normal between Descent and Before Landing, is kept on this device, is read aloud like any other and opens with “hey Aero, approach checklist”.
Say procedure and the wake word understand plain names: landing, takeoff, start, shutdown, cruise, descent, taxi, climb, approach, and any procedure title.
Status → Voice shows the wake listener's state and the last words it heard, and more mis-hearings of “Aero” (euro, zero, hero, arrow…) are accepted.
Checklists opened by voice are now read aloud (the speech engine is primed by your first tap) and start by naming the checklist. Saying the wake word on its own can no longer tick a line.
Wake-word commands wait until you have finished speaking and prefer the checklist whose full name you said. Speech after a voice command is more reliable on Apple devices.
A spoken request to open a checklist always reads it, even if Read aloud was off. Status → Voice has a voice log for troubleshooting.
Apple devices: listening now always stops before the app speaks, so voice-opened checklists are read; the listening tone sounds when the microphone is actually live.
Voice commands recognise Before Start, Descent and After Landing correctly (an exact checklist name now wins over shortcuts).
Spoken checklist names tolerate mis-hearings a letter or two off (for example “dessert” for Descent).

title: Voice: read aloud, spoken replies and recall
notes: Read aloud (Status → Voice): the app speaks each line of an open checklist, waits for ✓ Checked, then reads the next. Works offline and in Bluetooth headsets. Speaking rate and voice are selectable.

Voice replies (experimental): after each line the app listens for “checked”, “set”, “repeat”, “skip” or “stop”. What it heard is shown before anything is applied. Needs microphone permission and, on Apple devices, signal.
Say procedure: with voice replies on, a microphone button above each checklist list lets you say a procedure name, for example “engine failure in flight”, and the app opens it.
All of this is off by default; nothing changes unless you turn it on.
Status → Voice has a Test the microphone button that reports exactly what the device says, and the voice bar names the reason when listening fails.
Spoken replies are acted on as soon as the word is heard, without waiting for the end-of-speech pause.
Default speaking rate lowered, with five steps from Slow to Fast; tapping a step plays a sample.
Normal checklists are read in short form: the challenge and the capitalised action only, with bracketed detail left on screen. Can be turned off under Status → Voice.

Listening is more dependable: the microphone stays open for as long as a line is waiting, opens a fraction of a second after the voice finishes, and accepts more ways of saying checked. Cue tones (one when listening, two when accepted) can be turned off.
Confirm a line by saying “checked” or the written response itself, for example “both on” or “idle cutoff”. Other words no longer tick a line.
The microphone now opens while the line is being read, so a reply is caught the moment the voice stops; anything heard before that is ignored. Switchable under Status → Voice.

title: Send to EFB, and Mac window fix
notes: The EFB rows on each Status page are now Send to EFB buttons: they open the share sheet with the file attached, so Copy to OzRWY or Save to Files is one tap. On a computer the file opens in the browser to save from there.
EFB files show a banner saying what they are, with a Share this file button and a link back to the app, so they are not mistaken for the app's own checklist.
On Mac and iPad installs the header now clears the window's close, minimise and zoom buttons.
If an EFB file is requested with no signal, a short message appears instead of the app page.
Version is shown as a plain number (1.7) in the app and in the EFB files; the build code moves to small print.

title: User guide
notes: A user guide explaining installation, the picker and favourites, working through checklists, emergency procedures, the Status page, day and night display, updates, offline use, EFB files and troubleshooting. Linked from the picker and every aircraft's Status page, and available offline.
Fixed: opening the app with signal now reliably loads the newest page on the first launch (a fault in the page fetch meant it could take one extra launch).

title: EFB files inside the app, and release notes
notes: Each aircraft's Status page now has an EFB files section: an interactive single-file checklist and a printable PDF for loading into OzRunways or AvPlan, with instructions.
The update bars now say what changed, with a What's new button. The Status page has a What's new row.
Hot and flooded start branches added to the Maule M-6 and M-7 engine start.

title: 30 aircraft and faster updates
notes: Added GA8 Airvan, Maule M-6-235 and M-7-235, King Air B200, Conquest II, Cessna 310R, 402C, 210M and 210R, Navajo, Chieftain, Malibu, Matrix and PC-12/45.
Opening the app with signal now always fetches the newest build instead of a cached copy.
Update bars are coloured: amber when a new version is waiting, green once applied.

title: Favourites and update awareness
notes: Star an aircraft to pin it under Favourites; the app offers this after three opens.
A bar announces a downloaded update while the app is open and an applied update on the next launch; the Status page shows the version and a manual check.

title: Day and night modes, cockpit colours
notes: Header switch cycles Auto, Day and Night; remembered on the device.
Normal, Abnormal and Emergency tabs coloured green, amber and red; warnings red, cautions amber; next-item marker takes the tab colour.

title: Multi-aircraft app
notes: Aircraft picker with 16 common GA types, progress kept per aircraft, V-speeds page and deep links by aircraft id.

title: C208B offline checklist
notes: First installable version with the Cessna 208B checklists, saved progress and offline use.
